title:
Step 2 of 10:
Is it *GxP* at all?
sub: Half of what lands on QA's desk does not belong there. Knowing which half is how you earn trust.

title:
Saying yes to everything
looks careful.
text:
It is how QA becomes the queue everyone routes around. Teams stop asking, and you find out about the AI after it is live.

The fastest way to be included early is to be quick and clear about what you do not need to see.

title:
Three questions
settle most of it:
items: Does the output *create, change or inform a GxP record*?
Does a person make a *GxP decision* using it - release, deviation, CAPA, submission, patient safety?
Could a wrong output *reach product, patient or submission* before a human would notice?

title:
Follow the output,
not the tool.
text:
The same model is in scope in one place and out of it in another. What matters is where the output lands and who relies on it.

Ask where this output goes next. Keep asking until it either reaches a regulated record or it does not.
tag: Tools are not GxP. Uses are

title: The quick sort:
items: *In scope* - drafting a deviation summary that enters the record
*In scope* - generating validation test scripts, your own evidence
*In scope* - flagging anomalies a reviewer relies on
*Out of scope* - drafting a job advert, a slide deck, an internal email
*Out of scope* - summarising a meeting nobody cites as evidence
*Grey* - a chatbot over SOPs: no record, but it shapes what people do

title:
Out of GxP scope is not
out of scope entirely.
text:
Confidential data, personal data, IP leaving the company, security review, licence terms. All still apply.

Saying "not GxP" is not permission. It is a routing decision: this one goes to IT and security, not to validation.
tag: Say where it goes, not just that it leaves you

title:
Then write the decision
down. One line.
text:
What it is, in or out of GxP scope, the reason, who decided, the date.

That single line is the start of your AI inventory, and it is the answer when someone asks two years later why this was never validated.

title:
Step 3 next week:
classify what is left.
text:
In scope does not mean one treatment for everything. Next step is influence times consequence, and the four decisions that come out of it.

Follow along if this is useful, and forward it to whoever is answering these questions today.
